title: Structured Outputs: JSON, Schema Validation, Constrained Decoding

questions.question: Why is getting structured JSON output from LLMs challenging?
options: JSON Schema cannot express enums, nested objects, or typed array items, so most real output shapes cannot be described
Markdown code fences are appended by the API after generation, so the returned string is always wrapped and unparseable — and applies unchanged even when the lesson's stated preconditions fail
LLMs generate free-form text token by token and can produce invalid JSON (missing brackets, wrong types, extra text) at any point
Providers emit JSON only through tool use, so a plain completion call can never return an object however you prompt it
questions.explanation: LLMs generate tokens autoregressively. They might add a trailing comma, forget a closing bracket, include markdown formatting around JSON, or hallucinate extra fields. Each token is independent, so structural validity isn't guaranteed.

questions.question: What is constrained decoding?
options: Validating the finished response against a Pydantic model and retrying with the error message when parsing fails
Restricting which tokens the model can generate at each step to ensure the output conforms to a grammar or schema
Stripping markdown fences and preamble text out of the response before handing the remaining string to a JSON parser
Passing the JSON Schema inside the prompt text so the model can read the required keys and types before it answers
questions.explanation: Constrained decoding masks out invalid tokens at each generation step. After an opening brace, only valid JSON keys are allowed. After a colon, only valid value tokens. This guarantees structural validity at the token level.

questions.question: What is the benefit of using Pydantic models for LLM output validation?
options: They define typed schemas that automatically validate, parse, and reject malformed LLM outputs with clear error messages
They mask invalid tokens during generation, so the model is physically unable to emit a value of the wrong type
They catch hallucinated values by checking each extracted field against the source text before returning the object, because one plausible output is sufficient production evidence
They let the model pick which extraction function to call when several different schemas could apply to one input
questions.explanation: Pydantic enforces types, required fields, value constraints, and nested structures. When the LLM produces invalid output, Pydantic gives specific error messages that can be fed back to the model for self-correction.

questions.question: What should you do when the LLM returns invalid JSON despite instructions?
options: Raise the temperature on the retry so the model samples a different, less truncated continuation of the object
Flatten the schema to a single level and drop every required field so that any output the model produces validates
Repair the string with a regex that closes unbalanced brackets and strips the preamble text before parsing again
Implement a retry loop that sends the validation error back to the model as context for a corrected attempt
questions.explanation: A retry loop with error feedback works well: parse the output, catch validation errors, send the error message back as context ('Your output had this error: ... Please fix it'). Most models self-correct on the second attempt.

questions.question: When should you use the API's native JSON mode vs prompt-based JSON extraction?
options: Use native mode when valid structure must be guaranteed; use prompt-based when the model has to reason about what to extract
Use native JSON mode only for arrays and prompt-based for objects, since token masking cannot enforce item counts
Use prompt-based extraction for high-volume jobs, because native mode adds a second validation call and doubles cost — and applies unchanged even when the lesson's stated preconditions fail
Both paths end up equivalent once a Pydantic model validates the result, so pick whichever reads better in the code
questions.explanation: Native JSON mode (OpenAI's response_format, Anthropic's tool_use) guarantees valid JSON structure. Prompt-based extraction is more flexible for complex reasoning about which fields to populate. Use native mode when structure matters most.

questions.question: What is the best completion criterion for Structured Outputs: JSON, Schema Validation, Constrained Decoding?
options: Build a Pydantic validation layer that rejects malformed LLM outputs and retries with error feedback
Skip validation and trust the first plausible-looking output
Choose a production framework before defining the core mechanism, with no need to inspect intermediate results or test edge cases
Treat one successful example as proof that every edge case works
questions.explanation: “Build a Pydantic validation layer that rejects malformed LLM outputs and retries with error feedback” is one of this lesson’s stated outcomes; the other choices bypass its required reasoning or validation.
